_about: Every number and name on screen, with its source (see sources.md). Checked 2026-10-24.

origin._source: Wikipedia, Ballon d'Or: 'presented by French magazine France Football since 1956'; 'Stanley Matthews of England was the inaugural winner of the award.' 1956 Ballon d'Or: 'Stanley Matthews received the award on 18 December 1956'

matthews._source: Wikipedia, Stanley Matthews: born 1 February 1915; award on 18 December 1956 → 41 years (our arithmetic)

vote._source: ESPN, 24 Oct 2026: votes by 'selected international journalists', one per country from 'the top 100 nations in the FIFA men's world ranking'

yashin._source: Wikipedia, Ballon d'Or: 'Lev Yashin is the only goalkeeper to have won the award.' Wikipedia, Lev Yashin: won 1963; nicknamed 'the Black Spider'; 'distinctive all-black outfit'
yashin.name: Лев Яшин, СССР

records._source: Sports Illustrated, modified 22 Sep 2025: Messi '8 (2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2015, 2019, 2021, 2023)'; Ronaldo '5 (2008, 2013, 2014, 2016, 2017)'; Platini, Cruyff, van Basten '3' each. Wikipedia: 'Lionel Messi holds the record for most Ballon d'Or wins with eight.'

women._source: Wikipedia, Ballon d'Or Féminin: 'first awarded in 2018, with Ada Hegerberg of Norway'; Aitana Bonmatí won 2023, 2024, 2025: 'the first player to win it three times, and three times in a row'

next._source: ESPN, 24 Oct 2026: ceremony 'Monday, Oct. 26', London Palladium, 'held outside Paris for the first time'. Wikipedia, 2026 Ballon d'Or: '26 October 2026 at the London Palladium'
